name: The Higgs Field
description: Space is not empty, it is filled with a field of moving particles. The more particles, the stronger the field. In this context particle density is called mass.

name: Entropy
description: Entropy is the stable state of the universe. A single atom is more or less stable. Particle forces are equal in all directions. Click near the circle to create a vacuum. Select Show Particle Density to toggle the particle density to see the vacuuum (bending of 'space-time') around an atom.

name: Gravity (Lilje)
equation: $$F = P \cdot A \qquad P = nkT \qquad \Delta P = \text{shadow deficit}$$
description: Any two objects have relatively fewer particles between them due to occlusion, causing gravitational attraction. The more particles, the stronger the gravity. P = n k T  . The key is virtual particles - particle 'bubbles' that burst on contact. Karl Lilje 2016

name: Gravity Far
equation: $$F = P \cdot A \qquad P = nkT \qquad \Delta P = \text{shadow deficit}$$
description: Any two objects have relatively fewer particles between them due to occlusion and absorbtion by the nucleus, causing gravitational attraction. The more particles, the stronger the gravity. P = n k T  . Karl Lilje 2016

name: Gravity 2
description: Smaller atoms are more attracted to larger, more dense ones. Objects have relatively fewer particles between them due to occlusion and absorbtion by the nucleus, causing gravitational attraction. The more particles, the stronger the gravity. P = n k T  . Karl Lilje 2016

name: Gravity 3
equation: $$\mathbf{F}(\mathbf{x}) = \kappa(\mathbf{x}) \, p \, v \int_{4\pi} f_0 \, \exp\left(-\int_{0}^{\infty} \kappa(\mathbf{x} - s\,\Omega) \, ds\right) \Omega \, d\Omega$$
description: Objects have relatively fewer particles between them due to occlusion, causing gravitational attraction. The more particles, the stronger the gravity. P = n k T  . Karl Lilje 2016

name: Quantum Condensation
description: From nothing, something. Particles condense into a stable state, a quantum condensation process. Matter.

name: Flame Simulation
description: Fire is hollow

name: Double Slit Experiment
description: One packet of particles (a photon wave) creates two beams of light, with multiple obervable points

name: Global Illumination
description: This shows how even the darkest area can be illuminated even when there is no direct light path, as long as there are enough particles to find a path through the maze.

name: Cloud Chamber
description: Simulates a cloud chamber where particles are emitted from a radioactive source and interact with a sensor (observer). Occasionally pleasing collisions are observed, showing 'strange' paths.

name: Magnetic Fields
description: (WIP) Simulates magnetic fields and their interactions with a magnetised ferromagnetic material. The rectangles act like monotonically aligned metal crystal whose preferred direction gradually increases along the construct, shaping the surrounding particle flow. It take some time for the fields to emerge.

name: Photon Generation
description: A photon (a wave with a frequency we can detect) is generated by asymmetry of spinning atoms. The faster it rotates, the higher the frequency.

name: Photon Waves
description: An atom oscillates back and forth 'surfing the vacuum', disturbing the surrounding particle field and generating electromagnetic waves that propagate outward at the speed of light.

name: Solar System
description: A scaled representation of our solar system if we did not orbit the sun. Relative sizes are to scale (Sun radius = 109x Earth). Planets positioned at their correct relative orbital distances: Mercury (0.39 AU), Venus (0.72 AU), Earth (1.0 AU), Mars (1.52 AU), Jupiter (5.2 AU), Saturn (9.54 AU), Uranus (19.19 AU), Neptune (30.07 AU). After some time, the planets begin to orbit the sun.

name: Linear Accelerator
description: A linear particle accelerator (LINAC) that accelerates particles in a straight line through a series of accelerating cavities. Particles gain energy at each stage, reaching higher velocities as they progress through the accelerator.

name: Particle Accelerator
description: A circular particle accelerator that accelerates particles through electromagnetic fields. Particles gain energy as they pass through accelerator sections (rectangles) arranged in a ring pattern. Watch as particles spiral outward gaining speed, simulating a synchrotron or cyclotron.

name: Quantum Liquid
description: A 2D liquid simulation using Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics (SPH). Particles interact with each other through pressure, viscosity, and surface tension forces, creating realistic fluid behavior with gravity.

name: Wormhole
description: An atom travels through space. When it enters the hidden wormhole zone (center rectangle), it experiences reduced resistance and can travel at higher speeds, simulating faster-than-light travel through warped spacetime.

name: Rocket Engine (Newtonian)
description: (Contrived animation) Newton's Third Law in action. Mass is ejected backward at high speed from the rocket engine nozzle, and by conservation of momentum the rocket accelerates forward through the particle medium. The bright orange exhaust plume is the reaction mass — F = ṁvₑ.

name: Rocket Engine (Lilje)
description: Explains WHY Rocket propulsion happens through particle pressure. Simulates the importance of nozzle design to avoid particle vacuum and collapse. The rocket movement is emergent from particle interaction. Notice how the shockwave can actually push the rocket back down.

name: Gravity (Le Sage)
equation: $$F = P \cdot A \qquad P = nkT \qquad \Delta P = \text{shadow deficit}$$
description: Le Sage postulated that gravity is caused by the repulsion of atoms by the nucleus. (Le Sage 1748). However particle simulation proves no significant emergent gravitational phenomenon.

name: AntiGravity
description: Lowering the density of the particle field by evacuating particles causes objects to move toward the lower density area.
